To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Casimir-Liftshitz and Casimiter-Polder interactions with semiconductors are modified in the presence of charge drift, which is a general feature of any material with a finite conductivity.

(i) the Casimir-Liftshitz and Casmir-Polder interactions with semiconductors are modified by the presence of drifting electrons in the bulk material, and (ii) the resulting frequency-dependent dispersion relations coincide with those recently derived for the thermal Lifshiz force with conducting surfaces in the quasistic limit

(i) the Casimir-Lifshtiz and Casimir-Polded interactions of a neutral body with semiconductor surfaces are affected by the presence of charge carriers in the bulk; (ii) the Casimir force is enhanced by the presence of carriers, while the thermal Casimir force is weakened by the presence of a carrier density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the Casimir-Liftshitz and Casimr-Polder forces with semiconducting materials.
the study of quantum vacuum effects in the presence of materials.
the development of a new theory for the Casimir-Liftshitz and Casimmer-Polder interactions with semiconductors and insulators that accounts for the charge drift in the material.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Lifshitz formula for dielectrics and the Debye-Langevin formula for conductors are both special cases of a general formula, which includes the effects of charge drift and thermal fluctuations.
the Casimir-Lifshtiz force for a dielectric surface is given by Eq. (3) and that the Casimir-Polder force for a dielec-tric surface in the quasitatic limit is given by Eq.(5).

the Casimir-Liftshitz and Casimiter-Polder interactions with semiconductors or insulators are not only determined by the dielectric response of the bulk material but also depend on the charge drift in the material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first complete theory for the thermal Casimir force between semiconductor surfaces that takes into the account charge drift.

the Casimir-Polder and Casimir-Lifshitiz interactions between a polarizable atom or a dielectric sphere and a semiconductor surface are determined by the same frequency dependent dielectric permittivity that is used to describe optical properties of semiconductors.

the Casimir-Liftshitz interaction between two semi-conducting or insulating materials is not only determined by the dielectric permittivity of the bulk material but also by the drift velocity and density of the free carriers.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, when the carrier density is small, the thermal Casimir-Lifhsitz interaction is dominated by a contribution from the drift of the carriers, while the Casimir-Polder interaction is dominated by the drift of the electrons.
the Casimir-Polder and Casimir-Lifschitz interactions with semiconductor surfaces can differ from those with dielectric surfaces.
for semiconductors and insulators the Casimir-Liftshitz and Casimiter-Polder interactions are dominated by the contribution from the drift of the carriers.
